posts.text:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent related

Here's basically everything you need to know about building a Grok Bot quality AI agent:

1. Agents are split between routers and workers. The user talks to the router, then gives the work to the workers. The router never does work. This is why the chief of staff model in Grok Bot works SO well

2. Proactive means acting on events, not chats. The agent should always be watching for events and react based on every event that comes through it. Routing to the right worker/action

3. Messages should be in a queue. Users should be able to send messages even while the agent is working, and each message queues/steers the agent

4. Besides the router and workers, there should be a watchdog layer. The watchdog makes sure the agent is always up and fixes it when there are issues. This is why Hermes succeeded and OpenClaw struggled. Constantly broke and couldn't fix itself

5. Protect human attention. Only message the user when it needs to act or the user can use the result. Lighten their cognitive load. Another thing Grok Bot is excellent at. When you message it you can be confident the next message you get will be it saying the task is complete.

posts.text_zh:
DeepSeek 刚把做 AI Agent 的关键秘密摊开了。

如果你在做任何 Agent 相关的事，这篇文章极重要。关于打造 Grok Bot 级 Agent，你基本上需要知道这些：

1. Agent 拆成路由与工人。用户只跟路由说，路由派活给工人，自己从不下场——这就是 Grok Bot「幕僚长」模式好用的原因。
2. 主动不等于多聊天，而是盯事件：每条事件来了就路由到正确工人/动作。
3. 消息要进队列：Agent 忙着时用户仍可发消息，每条都能排队/纠偏。
4. 除了路由和工人，还要有看门狗层，保证 Agent 一直活着、出问题能自修——Hermes 成、OpenClaw 常挂，差别就在这。
5. 保护人类注意力：只在需要用户行动或结果可用时才打扰。

抽出一小时认真读原文。

AI 奇怪的视觉能力

来自 Google DeepMind 的研究论文，探索了简单视觉图形如何悄悄操纵多模态 AI 的决策行为。

他们发现，多模态 AI 在看图时脑回路很怪，人类很难摸清一张无关的图片到底会对 AI 的判断产生什么隐蔽影响。

拿 Claude Opus 4.7、Gemini 3.1 Pro 和 GPT-5.4 做对照实验，在写代码、文字创作等任务里塞入红心、三角、箭头等 288 种基础彩色符号，或者用 Python 代码画画，观察 AI 行为变化并抓取它们内部的思考痕迹。

测试发现，一张看似毫无关联的红心图片，能直接让原本偏好循环写法的 AI 百分之百改用递归写法；圆圈则会诱导 AI 优先选择环形缓冲区。AI 则完全意识不到被影响了，它们在内部思考链里声称这纯属巧合或给出一堆看似专业的借口。两台 AI 互相用图画沟通时，往往会形成人类完全看不懂的怪异暗号，但彼此却能秒懂对方的意思。

论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36449

Every model upgrade makes AI apps cheaper to run, and easier for customers to replace.

Still, 94% of enterprise LLM buyers expect their spend to rise.

Three rules for winning that spend over the build-it-yourself option:

1. Operate the workflow better than the customer can
2. Make context cheaper to rent than to rebuild
3. Prove the value, then price to capture it

Who's doing it:

- Legal AI platform Harvey beat a general-purpose AI assistant and energy giant Repsol's own in-house tool in a blind test

- Notion considered building its own support AI, then bought Decagon’s AI support agents so its team could stay focused on the core product

"Model progress continually improves the customer's alternative. Your advantage must widen faster for the application to keep earning its premium."

Full piece from a16z's Tugce Erten: https://www.a16z.news/p/how-ai-applications-earn-their-premium

DecisionRAG：用决策模型实现快速且精准的搜索

非常巧妙的思路，用Jev类决策模型来代替传统的搜索排序工具。这个方法借鉴了人类在图书馆查书的习惯，把庞大的资料库整理成大分类、文章标题到具体段落的层级结构。决策模型不需要逐字生成文本，只需在单次计算中对同级的所有选项同时打分，逐层筛选出最有价值的分支。

实际测试中，即使面对维基百科超过 268 万个段落的庞大资料库，系统也能在 0.7 到 1.8 秒内完成精准查找，单次查询成本只有 0.2 到 2.3 美分。在多个问答测试集上，这项技术不仅比传统搜索加重排方案的准确率高出十几个百分点，还比让普通大模型慢慢思考查找快了 30 多倍。

论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35868

同时开 5 个 Agent，人就盯不过来了

DeepSeek Harness 团队公开了一套 Super-agent 设计，思路很直接：session 别让人管了，交给系统。

你只跟同一个 Agent 说话，它在后台同时推进好几件事。

核心是两层：

Router 只负责沟通和派活，连 Bash 都不给它，用便宜的快模型

Worker 每个只做一件事，用最强的模型，但不许直接跟人说话，报错和工具日志全锁在里面，你在群里只看到 Router 整理过的结论

群里的消息先过代码规则
闲聊群直接丢掉，0 token
剩下的才交给轻量模型判断要不要管

有人在群里吐槽一个 macOS 的 bug，没 @ 它
它自己在后台复现，定位到 Electron 的 detail=2 机制，带着前后对比截图提了 PR

最有意思的是实验：

单会话 + 中立提示词，5 轮全是模型自己下场干，一个子任务都没派出去

换成强委派提示词，还是有 1 轮觉得任务小、自己干了

结果 p95 拖到 29 分钟，Super-agent 是 15.7 分钟

结论：想让模型分活，靠 Prompt 劝不住，得在架构上把它的手拿掉

代价也写得清楚：每轮 token 23.2M，单会话方案是 6.1M 和 10.8M

还有两个细节：

同一个 PR 的后续消息直接推给负责的 Worker，不再经过 Router。关掉这条直通，token 多花 37%

事件越密集越省：每分钟从 1 个涨到 40 个，单次决策反而从 6.4 秒降到 1.6 秒

大脑放在云端，你电脑上只跑一个轻量 daemon
笔记本合盖它照样盯群和 PR，第二天开机自动补跑本地测试

最大的坑还没填：它常驻、读公开群聊和外部 PR，又连着你的电脑。被 Prompt 注入一次，连着的设备都可能被接管

你敢让这样一个 Agent 常驻，还连着自己的开发机吗？

Blacksmith (W24) is building a faster cloud for continuous integration (CI), helping developers test and ship code as AI coding tools generate more of it.

As software production accelerates, testing and validation are becoming the new bottleneck. That shift has helped @useblacksmith grow 20x over the last year, and the company recently raised a $66 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation.

The founders, @adijayaprakash, @aayush_shah15, and @adityamaru27, started as outsiders to DevOps and built their first infrastructure using the same high-performance CPUs found in gaming PCs, renting servers originally designed for Minecraft and Call of Duty. Today, they run a much larger fleet with a team of just 30 people, helping companies cut CI waits from minutes to seconds. 

They share how they found the idea, won their first 200 customers, and why faster testing will become even more important as agents write more of the world’s code.

03:46 — Winning Over Investors and Developers
06:46 — Scaling CI for the AI Coding Era

Bridgit Mendler of @NorthwoodSpace says the builders of the early internet bet on a direction without knowing exactly what it would become, and the space industry is in that same moment now:

"For folks that were early with the internet, there's no way they would've foreseen what the internet is today. But they were betting on a direction... and look what we have today."

"I think we're in a similar moment with the space industry where we don't know what is going to be built. A year ago today, would we think that everybody would be talking about orbital data centers? No way."

"But it's captivated the public imagination and who knows what's gonna come next... The whole thing that we're about is taking companies further faster. Taking space missions further faster."

"If you analogize to the internet, you have a couple of kind of platform infrastructure plays that really wind up becoming enmeshed across the internet... There are a few that wind up becoming really influential and fundamental."

"Cloud is one that we analogize to a lot and we are inspired by. And we wanna be one of those companies."

@BridgitMendler

Viewer discretion advised. This is a 3 minute real time replay of the Florida Learjet 60 crash, with the uncut ATC audio.

It pulls together public ADS-B, weather radar, satellite, dashcam and drone video onto one timeline.

Here's what we know as of Nov 2 based on OSINT and today's NTSB briefing:

- Went from ~35,000 ft to impact in ~78 seconds
- Flew into a string of thunderstorms
- Crew reported ice and turbulence; asked to climb then issued a mayday
- All nine aboard are deceased, with one person injured on the ground
- Plane debris spread across half a mile and still being recovered
- NTSB says there is some evidence the jet broke up before impact
- Weather at altitude is a key focus of the investigation; but the official cause is still TBD

I make a lot of 4D reconstructions and this is the most visceral and gut wrenching thing I’ve heard in a long time. My heart goes out to the families of those on board. Important to note that the details so far point to severe weather at altitude rather than a missile or air defense system.
